name: Wave Director
summary: Endless escalating waves, a boss on a cadence, and the stall-breaker that stops a wave being unfinishable.
description: Owns the shape of a run and nothing about its content: how much a wave is worth, when to spend it, when it is over, when a boss is due, and what to do when a wave will not end. A wave is a budget rather than a headcount, so content prices its own spawns and a wave gets harder without simply getting longer; the budget converts into spawns no faster than they are cleared, which turns a late wave from one unaffordable blob into sustained pressure and doubles as a frame-cost ceiling. It stops between waves rather than rolling on, because between waves is where a draft, a shop or a breather goes. There is no last wave: bosses cycle and the budget keeps climbing, so a run ends when the player does.
nextSteps: Put WaveDirector.js on one manager actor and tag it Waves.
Set contentTag to the script that will do the spawning.
Implement spawnOne(wave, budgetLeft) returning what the spawn cost, and aliveCount().
Implement onWaveCleared(wave, isBoss) and call resume() when the player has finished choosing -- nothing starts the next wave for you.
